title: Mind captioning: text descriptions of viewed videos decoded from fMRI
summary: In six participants, a language-model pipeline translated fMRI responses to viewed videos into descriptions of their semantic content. Video identification reached about 50% among 100 candidates, compared with 1% chance. Results also extended to instructed video recall and persisted when the canonical language network was excluded, supporting a shared semantic representation beyond that network. The experiment used extensive participant-specific training; it was not unrestricted reading of private thoughts or a clinical aphasia trial.
ai_technology: Deep language model semantic-feature decoder with text generation search

evidence.tested: Video viewing and instructed recall in six participants; 2,180 unique videos in training and comparisons with analyses excluding the canonical language network.
evidence.unknown: Small participant group and extensive per-person training. Clinical communication benefits and arbitrary private-thought decoding were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Linear decoders mapped fMRI signals to deep-language-model semantic features; a language model guided text optimization.
